newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Novartis expects solid profit gain in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Novartis expects solid profit gain in 1997.

text.p: Swiss pharmaceuticals and life sciences giant Novartis AG said on Tuesday it expected operating profit and net profit to grow sharply in 1997, but gave no detailed forecast.
It also pleased investors by proposing raising its dividend to 20 Swiss francs ($13.7) per share from 16.80, giving its shares a boost of around one percent in pre-bourse trading.
"There is strong demand for shares," one dealer said.
Novartis, formed by the merger of Ciba-Geigy AG and Sandoz AG last year, said in a statement on its 1996 results that it expected most of the integration to be finished this year.

"Implementation of the merger is progressing well, with the majority of integration projects expected to be completed in 1997. In parallel, growth of established key products continues to be strong and new, innovative products are rapidly increasing their importance thanks to an aggressive programme of product launches already under way," it said.
Analysts have said they were keen for information on the group's product pipeline in view of the fact that many of its products, particularly those inherited from Ciba-Geigy, are quite mature.

"We anticipate a continued upward trend in top-line growth, with sales across all sectors and in most regions expected to grow dynamically. In 1997, we should also experience a strong positive currency effect," it said.
"Together with the realisation of the merger synthesis, this should lead, barring any unforeseen events, to a marked improvement of operating and net income."

Financial analysts had been waiting for word on how the merger was progressing because the company had already said 1996 profit would be in line with 1995 levels excluding exceptional costs and income related to the merger.
Novartis reported a 1996 net profit of 2.30 billion Swiss francs, down from 4.22 billion in 1995. Excluding exceptional items, 1996 net rose two percent to 4.18 billion from 4.10 billion.

Sales in the core life sciences business -- pharmaceuticals, agribusiness and nutrition -- rose eight percent to 27.60 billion Swiss francs. Total sales including divested operations rose to 36.23 billion from 35.94 billion.
It said operating income rose by four percent in 1996 and the merger had limited impact on margins.

"I am satisfied with the increase in operating income," Chief Financial Officer Raymund Breu said in the statement, "The merger process proceeded well with limited impact on our margins, which at 20.4 percent are in line with our expectations."
Group research and development (R&D) spending rose by four percent. R&D spending in the pharmaceuticals sector was maintained at 19 percent of sales.
Marketing expenditures increased seven percent for launches of fast-growing products as well as for additions to the sales force, the Novartis statement said. ($ = 1.459 Swiss Francs)
